subject.title: [Bug]: iOS app fails to connect over Tailscale CGNAT (100.x.x.x) — wss:// required but WebSocket upgrade silently dropped

question: Should native iOS remote Tailscale pairing remain TLS-only and be repaired through Serve/native TLS diagnostics, or may Tailnet CGNAT get a documented plaintext exception?
rationale: Current code, tests, and docs intentionally keep mobile Tailnet/public pairing on `wss://`, but the documented Serve/node path and live repro show users can still be blocked without a working secure handshake; changing this requires security-boundary intent.

options.title: Keep TLS-only and repair the secure path
options.body: Preserve Tailnet plaintext fail-closed behavior, then fix iOS/Tailscale Serve or native TLS diagnostics and prove a real iOS secure WebSocket pairing run.

options.title: Approve a narrow plaintext Tailnet exception
options.body: Allow `ws://100.64.0.0/10` only under explicit product/security approval with tests, docs, and upgrade-safe UI warnings.

options.title: Document direct CGNAT as unsupported
options.body: Leave direct Tailnet binds as a web/control or advanced path and steer mobile remote pairing to Tailscale Serve/Funnel or a configured `wss://` URL.

recommendation.title: Keep TLS-only and repair the secure path
recommendation.body: Preserve Tailnet plaintext fail-closed behavior, then fix iOS/Tailscale Serve or native TLS diagnostics and prove a real iOS secure WebSocket pairing run.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about the TLS trust and Gateway pairing security boundary where this history is strongest.
